description: A lane's workflow.yaml under workflow contract 1, generated from the contract registry: each key's own value. The rules across keys, the step definitions, skills and placeholders are the lane loader's (`pf workflows validate`); docs/reference/workflow-contract.md.

acceptance.description: required|none (default required): whether a work item on the lane must list an acceptance criterion before it runs

children_branch.description: string: the branch-name template the daemon checks a sub-ticket of this lane's work items out on — it must carry {seq} (the parent's seq), may carry {project} (the parent's project name), and its substituted name must be a legal git branch ref (WFC-112 otherwise)

tiers.description: map <tier> -> []<harness>:<model>[:<effort>]; the table a step's model_tier names

epic.description: bool (default false): the lane's own work items are epics — the lane must also declare children_branch and resume_reset (WFC-112 otherwise), and a first claim checks such a work item out on the children branch substituted with its own seq, records no fixed target (it merges into the origin's default branch) and snapshots its children

exclusive.description: bool (default false): one unfinished work item per project on the lane — a create on it reaches aihub exclusive, refused while another is not wrapped, failed or canceled

max_rewinds.description: int >= 0; required when any step declares on_fail, refused otherwise

resume_reset.description: string: the step id an owner-resumed epic's changed-children marker resets the lane to — required when the lane declares epic, refused without it, and it must name a step of this lane (WFC-112 otherwise)

tool_minutes.description: int > 0, <= 180, <= wall_minutes when both are declared: the step's own tool window

facts_proof.description: map {result, command} (default none): the mechanical facts summary this step's done needs for each task repo it changed (polyforge#241) — a `pf-step-result/1` file `facts.py handoff` writes, verdict pass whose heads carry the repo at its current HEAD; a repo the step did not change and a fast-forward need none; its refusal names every hit beside the result file

command.description: string, required: one line carrying {repo} (WFC-112 otherwise): the command a refusal quotes to write a fresh proof

result.description: string, required: the result file's path relative to the capsule, carrying {repo} (WFC-112 otherwise)

fast_check_proof.description: map {result, command} (default none): the fast-check proof this step's done needs for each task repo it changed — a `pf-step-result/1` file with verdict pass whose heads carry the repo at its current HEAD; a repo the step did not change and a fast-forward need none

command.description: string, required: one line carrying {repo} (WFC-112 otherwise): the command a refusal quotes to write a fresh proof

result.description: string, required: the result file's path relative to the capsule, carrying {repo} (WFC-112 otherwise)

hub.description: map {verbs, attrs} (default none): what the step may call through `pf step hub`

attrs.description: []attrs key (^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$), each at most once (default none): the top-level attrs keys the step may write (`pf step hub attrs <wi> --set <key>`); listing one lets the step call attrs, and the daemon refuses a write of any other key

verbs.description: []get|list|file|wrap-attrs|batch, each at most once (default none): the `pf step hub` verbs the step may call

human_mergeable.description: bool (default false): a project may declare the step's work done by a person with `steps.<project>.<step>.by: human` in its workspace yaml, fixed when the work item is first claimed; the step then asks the owner to do its work instead of running it itself, and a claim of a lane that does not declare the step human_mergeable is refused naming it

model_tier.description: a tier of defaults.tiers; exclusive with model_candidates

params.description: map <name> -> a single-line string (the lane default): the step's declared parameters. <name> is ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$, collides with no var or fragment (WFC-195), and a parameter the definition's placeholders never use is allowed (a script reads it); a value is one line of at most 256 bytes (WFC-112). The final value is composed at EVERY dispatch — lane default < the project's steps.<project>.<step-id>.params.<name> in its workspace yaml < the work item's pf override — fills the definition's {{<name>}} and reaches the step's scripts as PF_PARAM_<NAME>

resources.description: map {admission, locks}: what the daemon takes for the step's dispatch

admission.description: none|heavy (default none): a heavy-run admission slot for the dispatch

locks.description: []merge: the task repos' per-repo merge locks

rewind_only.description: bool (default false): the step runs only after a rewind covers it — the first round records it skipped without a dispatch, and it runs once any rewind that covers it (a gate FAIL's or an owner's) resets it to pending; a project skip of a `skippable` it declares wins over it, and the loader refuses the declaration when no gate's [on_fail target, gate) range covers the step (WFC-112)

skill.description: skill name: <lane>/skills/<name>.md, else _shared/skills/<name>.md, rendered into the prompt

skippable.description: bool (default false): a project may switch the step off with `steps.<project>.<step>.skip: true` in its workspace yaml, fixed when the work item is first claimed; a switched-off step is never dispatched (its execution status is skipped), and the wrap_attrs of skipped steps at the lane's end pass to the last step that runs

vars_files.description: map <var> -> a file of the lane (fragments/<name>.md), relative to the lane directory and inside it: the var's value is the file's text, exactly as if written in vars; a var is declared in vars or in vars_files, not both

waivable.description: bool (default false), gate only: the gate may hand off waive on the owner's word

wrap_attrs.description: []attr name (^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$), each at most once (default none): the wrap attrs the step registers (`pf step hub wrap-attrs <name>`) before its round may hand off done; listing one lets the step call wrap-attrs. When the steps at the lane's end are skipped (a skippable step a project switched off), their wrap_attrs are the last running step's to register

uncounted_rewinds.description: map {reason_contains, max}: the lane-declared class of gate-FAIL rewinds charged to no budget — a gate FAIL whose one-line hand-off reason carries reason_contains rewinds without spending max_rewinds, counted on its own toward max (the default 2 when the lane declares none; 0 = every matching FAIL asks the owner first, exactly like a spent max_rewinds); allowed only when a step declares on_fail, refused otherwise

max.description: int >= 0 (the default 2 when the lane declares none): the class's own rewind budget, held at `pf step handoff` exactly like max_rewinds

reason_contains.description: string, required, non-empty: the substring a gate FAIL's one-line hand-off reason carries when its rewind falls in the class (the stable prefix of the failing step's script summary; the rest of the line varies)

title: workflow.yaml (workflow contract 1)
